answer: Sybil defense: quadratic entry pricing. Each new identity burns a fee growing with the square of identities funded from one source per epoch. A registrar links applicants via a cipher - hash of funding address plus epoch seed - so splitting deposits across wallets cannot dodge it. Buying n seats costs about n squared; one honest agent pays once. The burn is the teeth: a clone farm drains its treasury faster than it gains influence. The public formula keeps the fee curve crystal clear: honest newcomers stay cheap, only the attacker's bill explodes. No island of cheap clones survives that.
